name: Word Counter & Text Statistics
title: Word Counter & Text Statistics — Live Unicode Counts
description: Count words, grapheme-based characters, sentences and paragraphs. See reading and speaking time, keyword density for one-to-three-word phrases and an optional progress goal.
intro: Type, paste or open a text file to see live counts. Character totals use grapheme clusters, so a combined emoji counts as one character, and word counting uses Unicode-aware tokenisation.
instructions: Type or paste text, or load a plain-text or Markdown file.
Read the primary statistics on the left and keyword density on the right.
Switch phrase length between one, two and three words, and toggle common-word filtering.
Set an optional word or character goal to see progress.

example.input: Hello world. This is a test.

faqs.a: Text is split into lines and tokens; punctuation at token edges is removed and tokens containing at least one letter or number count as words. Languages that do not use spaces are handled with browser word segmentation where available.

faqs.q: Are emoji counted as one character?
faqs.a: Yes. Character counts use grapheme clusters via Intl.Segmenter when available, so a joined emoji sequence is counted as one visible character.
No. This build keeps text in memory for the current page only. Closing or refreshing the page clears it.
It is a heuristic. Common abbreviations are handled, but unusual punctuation can still be counted differently from a human reader.

controls.label: Ignore common stop words in keyword density

article.heading: What the numbers mean
paragraphs: Words are tokens containing at least one Unicode letter or number. Characters are grapheme clusters rather than raw code units, which is why an accented letter or a flag emoji counts as a single character. Letters count Unicode letter code points, and unique words are case-insensitive.
Reading time assumes 238 words per minute and speaking time assumes 150 words per minute. Both show at least one second when any word is present.

article.heading: Keyword density rules
paragraphs: Density is calculated for one, two or three word phrases inside sentence-like segments. Common words can be excluded, numeric-only single words are skipped, and phrases must appear at least twice. Results are sorted by frequency and then alphabetically, with the top ten shown.

name: Text Cleaner
title: Text Cleaner — Remove Unwanted Characters, Spaces and HTML
description: Clean messy text in one ordered pass: trim whitespace, strip HTML tags and emoji, remove accents, unify quotes, fix punctuation and expand shorthand. Everything runs in your browser.
intro: Pick the rules you need from five groups, then clean the text in the reference tool’s processing order. An undo button restores the previous result, and a Default preset selects the commonly used rules.
instructions: Paste the text you want to clean, or type directly into the input box.
Choose options under Whitespace, Characters, HTML, Other text and Text formatting.
Use All, None or Default to set many options at once.
Click Clean Text. The result appears on the right; use Undo to step back.

faqs.a: No. Cleaning happens entirely in your browser. Nothing is sent to a server.

faqs.q: Does Strip emoji remove every emoji?
faqs.a: No. It targets the common pictograph ranges used by the reference tool, so some modern emoji, flags and joined sequences can remain. Use the Remove Emojis tool for the broader Unicode-range filter.

faqs.q: What does the Default preset select?
faqs.a: It selects trim, remove leading and trailing spaces, strip HTML tags, strip emoji, collapse multiple spaces and reduce multiple blank lines. It leaves letter case unchanged.
Yes. The Undo button restores the previous result. It is a simple history for this tool, not a full text-editor undo stack.

article.heading: A fixed processing order
paragraphs: Text Cleaner applies rules in a defined sequence: whitespace first, then character filters, HTML and decoding, links, and finally formatting. This matters because rules can interact. For example, stripping HTML tags before removing extra spaces produces different output from doing it the other way around.
The order in this build follows the supplied reference application so that results are predictable for people moving between the two tools.

article.heading: Honest limitations
paragraphs: HTML rules use regular expressions rather than a real HTML parser. Tag stripping removes anything between angle brackets, and attribute removal only matches quoted values. The “Strip emoji” option covers a small set of Unicode blocks and also treats literal pipe characters as literal characters, matching the reference implementation.
If you need precise HTML sanitisation or complete emoji removal, use a dedicated tool instead. This page reproduce the reference behaviour, including its quirks.

name: Remove Extra Spaces
title: Remove Extra Spaces — Collapse Repeated Whitespace
description: Replace every run of whitespace, including tabs and line breaks, with a single space and trim the ends. Upload a .txt file or paste text and copy the cleaned result.
intro: A focused one-click whitespace cleaner. Every JavaScript whitespace character is collapsed, which means paragraphs become a single line — use Text Cleaner if you need line-aware options.
instructions: Paste text into the box or choose a .txt file (up to 5 MB). A selected file takes priority over pasted text.
Click Remove Extra Spaces.
Copy the result from the output box.

faqs.a: No. The reference rule collapses all whitespace into one space, so newlines and paragraphs are removed. Use Text Cleaner for options that preserve lines.

faqs.q: Does it trim the start and end?
faqs.a: Yes. After collapsing whitespace, leading and trailing spaces are removed.

faqs.q: Is there a file size limit?
faqs.a: Files larger than 5 MB are rejected so the page stays responsive. Text is read locally in your browser.

article.heading: One simple rule
paragraphs: This tool applies one regular expression: every sequence of whitespace characters becomes a single space, then the outer ends are trimmed. That includes ordinary spaces, tabs, carriage returns, line feeds and less common Unicode spaces.
It is deliberately simpler than Text Cleaner. If you need to remove blank lines but keep paragraphs, or convert spaces to tabs, use the full cleaner instead.

name: Remove Empty Lines
title: Remove Empty Lines — Clean Blank Lines in Text and Documents
description: Remove blank and whitespace-only lines from pasted text, TXT, CSV, Markdown or DOCX while preserving every real line and its formatting.
intro: A focused line-cleaning tool with file support. Lines containing only spaces or tabs are treated as empty; choose whether to keep one blank line between paragraphs.
instructions: Paste text or load a TXT, CSV, Markdown or DOCX file.
Choose whether to preserve one blank line between paragraphs.
Click Remove empty lines, then copy or download the result.

faqs.q: Will it change the order or formatting of real lines?
faqs.a: No. Only empty and whitespace-only lines are removed. Indentation, tabs, punctuation and all other characters on real lines stay exactly as they were.
It collapses each run of blank lines to a single empty line, so paragraphs stay visually separated without leaving stacks of empty lines.

faqs.q: Can I open a Word document?
faqs.a: DOCX files are read locally where the browser supports decompression. Only paragraph text is extracted; tables, columns and styling are not preserved. PDF and legacy .doc files are rejected with an explanation instead of being silently mangled.

controls.label: Keep one blank line between paragraphs

article.heading: What counts as an empty line
paragraphs: A line is empty when it contains nothing, or only spaces and tabs after the line break is removed. That means a line of indentation is treated the same as a completely blank line, which is what most people expect when cleaning pasted code, logs or documents. Every other line is copied verbatim, including its indentation and trailing spaces.
If you turn on the paragraph option, consecutive empty lines become a single blank separator and trailing blank lines at the end of the document are removed. The order of real lines never changes.

article.heading: Files, DOCX and honest limits
paragraphs: Text-like files such as TXT, CSV, TSV, Markdown, JSON and HTML are read as text. DOCX files are opened as ZIP archives in your browser, and the paragraph text inside word/document.xml is extracted with the browser’s XML parser. This needs browser support for raw DEFLATE decompression; if it is missing, the tool says so and suggests saving the file as text instead.

A DOCX is a layout format, so tables, columns, headers, footers and character styling are not kept. Only the extracted text is cleaned. PDF files would require a layout-aware parser and legacy .doc is a different binary format, so neither is guessed at. The tool shows a clear limitation rather than returning damaged text.

name: Remove Emojis from Text
title: Remove Emojis from Text — Unicode Range Filter
description: Strip emoji and pictographic symbols using the exact Unicode ranges of the reference tool. Upload a .txt file or paste text; a selected file takes priority over pasted input.
intro: A direct port of the reference emoji filter. It removes matching code-point runs and leaves other characters, spacing and line breaks untouched.
instructions: Paste text or choose a .txt file up to 5 MB.
Click Remove Emojis.
Copy the cleaned result.

faqs.a: No. The filter uses a broad range list, but joined emoji sequences and keycap marks can leave behind zero-width joiners or combining characters. Some non-emoji symbols in the same ranges are also removed.

faqs.q: Does a selected file override pasted text?
faqs.a: Yes. That matches the reference workflow: if a file is selected, its contents are processed instead of the pasted text.
No. Only matched code-point runs are removed. Whitespace and formatting are preserved.

article.heading: Why some artifacts remain
paragraphs: The reference filter matches ranges of Unicode code points rather than whole emoji grapheme clusters. A family emoji or a keycap number is built from several code points; removing the pictographs can leave a zero-width joiner or a combining mark behind.
This build keeps that behaviour for fidelity. Always review the output if the text will be published or shared.

name: Remove Punctuation
title: Remove Punctuation — Strip Punctuation Marks in Text and Documents
description: Remove all Unicode punctuation, common English marks or your own chosen characters from pasted text, TXT, CSV, Markdown or DOCX while keeping letters and numbers.
intro: Choose between all Unicode punctuation, a smaller common-English set, or a custom list of characters. Accented letters, numbers, emoji and line breaks are preserved.
instructions: Paste text or load a TXT, CSV, Markdown or DOCX file.
Choose All Unicode punctuation, Common English marks, or Custom characters.
In Custom mode, type the exact characters to remove, then copy or download the result.

faqs.q: Are emoji and non-Latin scripts kept?
faqs.a: Yes. Only punctuation characters are removed. Letters from every script, numbers, emoji, symbols, spaces and line breaks are kept.

faqs.q: What is the difference between all and common punctuation?
faqs.a: All uses the Unicode punctuation property and also removes marks such as curly quotes, em dashes and CJK punctuation. Common removes only the familiar English marks: . , ! ? ; : ' " ( ) [ ] { } - – — _ / \ @ # & * and the quotation variants.

faqs.q: Can I open a Word document?
faqs.a: DOCX files are read locally where the browser supports decompression and only their text is cleaned. Layout, tables and styling are not kept. PDF and legacy .doc files are rejected with an explanation instead of being silently mangled.

article.heading: Three ways to choose what gets removed
paragraphs: The default All mode looks at the Unicode punctuation property, so it handles straight and curly quotes, em and en dashes, ellipses, and punctuation from scripts beyond Latin. Common mode uses a shorter list of marks that are familiar in English prose, which is useful when you want dashes or apostrophes left alone. Custom mode removes exactly the characters you type into the box and nothing else.

Whitespace is never treated as punctuation. Spaces, tabs and line breaks stay where they are, so the shape of your paragraphs and lists survives the operation. That makes the output safe to paste into a spreadsheet or a plain-text editor.

article.heading: Documents and honest scope
paragraphs: Text-like files such as TXT, CSV, TSV, Markdown, JSON and HTML are read directly as text. DOCX files are opened as ZIP archives in the browser and the paragraph text is extracted from the document XML. If the browser cannot decompress the archive, the tool reports the problem and suggests saving the document as text instead.

Only text is processed. A DOCX file can contain tables, columns, text boxes, headers and character formatting; none of that layout is preserved. PDF files and legacy .doc files need parsers this browser tool does not include, so they are rejected clearly rather than guessed at.

name: Find and Replace
title: Find and Replace — Literal or Regular Expression Mode
description: Replace all occurrences of a literal string, or turn off case sensitivity to treat Find as a live regular expression with global and case-insensitive flags. Invalid patterns show a clear error.
intro: Two modes match the reference tool: a case-sensitive literal replace, and a regular-expression replace used when case sensitivity is off. Read the hint below the fields before using metacharacters.
instructions: Enter the text or pattern to find and its replacement.
Leave Case-sensitive on for a literal, case-sensitive replacement of every occurrence.
Turn it off to compile Find as a regular expression with the g and i flags.

faqs.a: Not as a separate control. The reference tool advertises whole-word search but does not implement it. In regex mode you can add word boundaries such as \b yourself.

faqs.q: Can I export the result to Word or HTML?
faqs.a: No. Export to Word or HTML is advertised in the reference description but is not implemented there either. This tool provides a result box and a copy button.

faqs.q: Why did my search match more than expected?
faqs.a: With case sensitivity off, Find is compiled as a regular expression. Characters such as . * + and ( ) are active pattern syntax. A literal mode is used when the checkbox is on.

article.heading: Two different matching engines
paragraphs: The case-sensitive branch uses literal string replacement, so every character in Find is matched exactly. The other branch passes Find directly to the regular-expression engine with global and case-insensitive flags.
That difference is intentional because it matches the supplied source. An invalid regular expression is caught and reported instead of throwing an uncaught browser error.

article.heading: Advertised but not implemented
paragraphs: The reference page mentions whole-word searching and Word or HTML export. Neither exists in its application code. This implementation does not add them silently; the FAQ above records the gap so you can choose another tool when you need those features.

instructions: Type a headline.

faqs.a: They are transliterated to ASCII where possible, for example café becomes cafe. Scripts such as Arabic and Chinese are kept as valid Unicode letters.

article.heading: Splitting and formatting
paragraphs: The input is trimmed once before splitting. Line mode splits on line feeds and drops blank lines, comma mode splits and trims each part, and custom mode uses the separator you provide. A custom separator cannot be empty.
Formatting is applied in order: bullets use a bullet character, numbered items use 1-based numbers, dashes use a hyphen, and custom prefixes are followed by a space.

name: Bionic Reading Converter
title: Bionic Reading Converter — Fixations, Saccades and Reading View
description: Bold the first part of each word with adjustable fixation strength and saccade skipping. Preview the result, copy formatted text, HTML or Markdown, download an HTML file and open a distraction-free reading view.
intro: Five fixation levels, every-word or every-nth-word bolding, fade, font, size, line height and themes are all live. The reading view supports Escape to close and keeps focus inside the overlay.
instructions: Paste text or load the built-in sample.
Set fixation strength, saccade skipping, fade, font, size, line height and theme.
Use the preview to judge the pattern, then open Reading view for continuous reading.
Copy formatted text, HTML or Markdown, or download a standalone HTML file.

faqs.q: Does it handle apostrophes and hyphens?
faqs.a: Apostrophes inside words are handled. Hyphens are not part of the word pattern in the reference source, so “well-known” is treated as two words and may be bolded unevenly when saccade skipping is on.
No. Processing is local. This build saves your text and settings in this browser’s local storage so the preview survives a refresh; clear the text to remove it from the saved state.

faqs.q: What do fixation and saccade mean?
faqs.a: Fixation strength controls how much of each selected word is bold, from about 20% to about 70%. Saccade controls how often a word is selected: every word, every second word or every third word.

article.heading: Unicode-aware word handling
paragraphs: Words are matched with Unicode letter, mark and number properties, with internal straight or curly apostrophes allowed. Numbers, URLs, email addresses and bare domains are left unbolded so links remain readable.

Fixation points are chosen by grapheme, so accented characters and many Indic conjuncts are not split awkwardly. The interface uses real bold elements in the preview and escapes all text before producing HTML or Markdown.

article.heading: Local persistence
paragraphs: Text and options are saved to local storage after a short delay. This is convenient, but it means the text remains on this device until you clear it. The downloaded HTML file contains only your own output and no third-party branding.

name: Rich Text / HTML to Markdown
title: Rich Text / HTML to Markdown Converter — Local, Safe Markdown
description: Convert pasted HTML, rich text, text files or DOCX text into clean Markdown with headings, links, lists, tables, code and emphasis preserved.
intro: Paste markup from a webpage or rich-text editor, or load a text-like file or DOCX. A local DOM-free parser produces Markdown and a safe preview built from DOM nodes.
instructions: Paste HTML or rich text, or load an HTML, TXT, CSV, Markdown or DOCX file.
Markdown source and a safe preview update automatically.
Copy the Markdown or download it as a .md file.

faqs.a: Headings, paragraphs, links, bold, italic, inline code, fenced code, ordered and unordered lists, nested lists, blockquotes, tables, horizontal rules, line breaks and images.

faqs.q: Is pasted script or styling executed?
faqs.a: No. Scripts, styles, SVG, iframes and unsafe attributes are discarded. The preview is built with text nodes and a small allow-list of safe elements, never with innerHTML containing your content.

faqs.q: Can I convert a Word document?
faqs.a: You can load a DOCX, but only its text is extracted. Tables, columns and styling are not kept. For a fully faithful layout conversion, export the document as HTML first.

article.heading: What the converter preserves
paragraphs: The converter reads the markup as text and walks it locally. Headings keep their level, links keep their destination and title, and emphasis becomes asterisks or underscores. Lists are nested with indentation, blockquotes get a leading marker, code blocks are fenced, and simple tables are emitted as pipe tables. Images keep their source and alt text.
Whitespace is normalised between inline elements so pasted rich text does not produce broken sentences. Entities such as ampersands and non-breaking spaces are decoded before the Markdown is written.

article.heading: Safety and honest limits
paragraphs: Nothing is uploaded and no remote service is called. Script, style, SVG, iframe, object and form elements are dropped, as are event-handler and javascript: attributes. The side-by-side preview is assembled from DOM nodes using a strict allow-list, so markup in your own input cannot run code or alter the page.

This is a pragmatic converter for common web markup, not a full HTML5-to-CommonMark implementation. Complex nested tables, definition lists and custom elements may be simplified. DOCX files are read as ZIP archives where the browser supports decompression; only paragraph text is extracted, so layout and styling are lost.

faqs.q: How large a text can I compare?

No. Only extracted text is compared. DOCX uploads provide paragraph text; tables, columns and styling are not part of the comparison.
No. PDF text extraction would require a layout-aware parser, so PDF and legacy .doc uploads are rejected with an explanation rather than guessed at.

article.heading: How the diff is calculated
paragraphs: Both sides are split into lines or words and compared with a longest-common-subsequence algorithm. Unchanged units are shown with a leading space, additions with a plus sign and removals with a minus sign. The summary counts added and removed units so you can see the size of the change at a glance.

The output is rendered with text nodes inside safe elements, so markup in either input is displayed as text and never executed. Each side can be swapped, cleared or filled from its own file input, which makes it practical to review two versions of a document without a separate editor.

article.heading: Text only, and a firm size limit
paragraphs: This tool compares text, not formatting. A DOCX upload is opened as a ZIP archive in the browser and its paragraph text is extracted; tables, columns, headers and styling are outside the comparison. The status line states this explicitly so nobody mistakes the result for a visual track-changes view.

A full LCS comparison grows with the product of the two input sizes, so each side is capped at 1,200 units. Larger inputs return a clear error rather than freezing the page. PDF and legacy .doc files are rejected because reliable extraction would require a parser this local tool does not ship.

faqs.a: DOCX files are read locally where the browser supports decompression and only their text is scanned. PDF and legacy .doc files are rejected with an explanation.

article.heading: What counts as a link
paragraphs: The extractor looks for explicit http and https URLs, www-prefixed addresses and bare domains with a sensible suffix. Each candidate is trimmed of surrounding punctuation and validated before it is kept, so a sentence ending in a period does not produce a broken link. Results are de-duplicated in the order they first appear, which makes it easy to compare a pasted block with a source list.

Schemes other than http and https are deliberately ignored. A mailto: address is an email, not a web link, and javascript: values are never emitted, which keeps the output safe to paste into a document or a browser address bar.

article.heading: Files, privacy and limits
paragraphs: Text-like files such as TXT, CSV, TSV, Markdown, JSON and HTML are read directly. DOCX files are opened as ZIP archives in the browser and the paragraph text is scanned from the document XML; if raw decompression is unavailable, the tool explains how to save the file as text instead.

Everything runs on your device. No URL is fetched, followed or resolved, so the tool never contacts the sites it finds. Only links written in the input are reported; links hidden behind shortened redirects or generated by scripts cannot be recovered from pasted text.

name: Text Filter
title: Text Filter — Highlight and Remove Whole Words Safely
description: Remove whole words and highlight others with safe DOM spans. Terms are comma separated, matched case-insensitively with word boundaries, and input HTML is never executed.
intro: Removals run first, then highlights. Each comma-separated term is trimmed and matched as a whole word, so punctuation at the edges can affect matches. All output is built with text nodes rather than innerHTML.
instructions: Paste the source text.
Type comma-separated words to highlight and words to remove.
Click Apply Filter. Yellow highlights and removals appear in the output.
Copy the plain output text when you are done.

faqs.a: Yes. The reference tool writes output with innerHTML, which can execute markup from pasted text. This build creates highlight spans and text nodes directly, so no input HTML is interpreted.

faqs.q: Does it match phrases or partial words?
faqs.a: Terms are wrapped in word boundaries and escaped, so only whole words match. A term beginning or ending with punctuation or a non-ASCII letter may not match at those edges.

faqs.q: What happens to spacing after removal?
faqs.a: Only the matched word is removed. Surrounding spaces stay exactly as they were, so double spaces can remain.

article.heading: Order of operations
paragraphs: Every removal term is applied to the working text in the order typed, followed by every highlight term. Because the passes are sequential, a later removal can act on text changed by an earlier one.
Matches are case-insensitive and use word boundaries. The original input text is never trimmed, and empty comma-separated terms are ignored.

name: Text Redactor
title: Redact Text — Mask Sensitive Data and Restore It Locally
description: Mask names, emails, phone numbers, card numbers and API keys with stable labels, copy the redacted text, then restore original values from a key. Detection is heuristic and key files contain the original data.
intro: Three steps: paste and redact, copy the masked text, then paste a reply to restore values. Custom terms and category switches are available; the redaction key is generated on your device.
instructions: Paste text or load a plain-text file, then choose which categories to hide.
Choose labels, realistic fake values or black bars, and add any custom words to hide.
Copy the redacted text and paste it into another service only if you are comfortable doing so.
Paste that service’s reply into step 3 and restore the original values using the in-memory key or a saved key file.

faqs.q: Is redaction the same as anonymisation?
faqs.a: No. Detection is heuristic, and writing style or context can still identify someone. Always review the redacted text before sharing it.

faqs.q: Does this tool send my text anywhere?
faqs.a: No. Detection, replacement and restoration happen in your browser. This tool makes no network requests.

faqs.q: What is inside a saved key?
faqs.a: The key contains the original values for every label. Treat the file as sensitive, store it privately and delete it when you no longer need it.
No. Black-bar mode is irreversible because the original characters are not written into the text. Use labels or fake values when you need restoration.

article.heading: How labels stay consistent
paragraphs: Detected values are normalised so the same email, phone number or secret always receives the same label within one session. Overlapping matches are resolved by priority, length and position, and custom words are expanded to align with detected spans.
Restoration replaces bracketed labels and bare labels from the key. Fake values are mapped back as well; unknown labels are reported and left unchanged.

article.heading: Limits and safety
paragraphs: The reference tool caps uploads at 20 MB and internal scanning at one million characters, with lower caps for highlighted paths. This build applies a 5 MB upload limit for responsiveness.

Redaction reduces risk but cannot guarantee privacy. Check the output for anything the detectors missed, and remember that any service you paste redacted text into receives the redacted version, not the original.

name: Lorem Ipsum Generator
title: Lorem Ipsum Generator — Paragraphs, Sentences, Words and Lists
description: Generate placeholder text by paragraphs, sentences, exact words or list items with classic or standard styles and plain text, HTML or Markdown output. Generation caps apply per unit.
intro: Choose a unit and amount, select a style and format, then generate. The classic style draws from a Latin-like vocabulary; the standard style cycles four canonical sentences.
instructions: Pick a quick amount or set an amount and unit manually.
Choose classic or standard style and plain, HTML or Markdown output.
Toggle the opening sentence and paragraph wrapping as needed.
Copy or download the generated text. Regenerate for a new variation.

faqs.a: No. The reference description says there is no limit, but the application caps output at 100 paragraphs, 500 sentences, 5,000 words or 100 list items depending on the unit.

faqs.q: Can I get an exact word count?
faqs.a: Yes. Choose the Words unit and enter the number you need. The generator slices to exactly that many words.

faqs.q: What is the difference between classic and standard?
faqs.a: Classic builds sentences from a pool of Latin-like words and avoids repeats within a sentence. Standard cycles the four classic Lorem ipsum sentences, optionally starting partway through the passage.

article.heading: Units, styles and formats
paragraphs: Paragraphs contain several sentences, sentences are single blocks, words are sliced to an exact count, and list items can be plain bullets, HTML lists or Markdown bullets. Classic style chooses random words from a 179-word vocabulary; standard style reuses fixed passages.
HTML output can wrap paragraphs in paragraph tags, and list output can use ordered or unordered HTML lists. Preview and Source tabs show the rendered and raw versions respectively.

article.heading: Why the caps exist
paragraphs: The caps mirror the supplied reference tool and keep generation responsive. They are documented here rather than hidden, because the reference page advertises unlimited output. Choose the largest permitted amount for long mock-ups, or run the generator more than once.

name: Text to Handwriting
title: Text to Handwriting — Convert Text to Handwritten Pages
description: Turn typed text into realistic handwriting on notebook paper and export as PNG or multi-page PDF. Already built and preserved.
intro: This existing browser tool renders your text with handwriting fonts and paper styles, then exports PNG or PDF. Its original URL and functionality are preserved.
instructions: Open the handwriting converter.
Type or paste your text and choose a font and paper style.
Export as PNG or PDF.

faqs.a: No. The existing tool renders and exports entirely in your browser.

name: AP Case Converter
title: AP Case Converter — Title Case, Abbreviations and Numerals
description: Apply a regex-based AP-style pass to text: title case, short-word lowercasing, month and state abbreviations, sentence starts and single-digit numerals. Each rule can be switched off.
intro: Six switches mirror the reference tool. The rules run in a fixed order, and the result appears below the input for copying.
instructions: Paste or type the text to convert.
Toggle any of the six AP style rules.
Click Convert to AP Style and review the output.
Copy the result.

faqs.q: Is this a complete AP style checker?
faqs.a: No. It is a shallow regex pipeline covering title case, short words, sentence starts, month and state abbreviations and single-digit numerals. It does not handle titles, dates, times, currencies or Washington, D.C.

faqs.q: Why does Lowercase short words stop working when title case is off?
faqs.a: In the reference source that rule is nested inside the title-case rule. This build preserves the behaviour. Turn title case on if you need short words lowercased.

faqs.q: Does sentence capitalisation understand question marks?
faqs.a: No. The reference rule only looks for a period followed by whitespace, so question marks, exclamation marks and newlines do not start a new sentence.

article.heading: Six ordered rules
paragraphs: The converter title-cases ASCII words, lowercases a fixed list of short words, capitalises the first character after a period, shortens month names, shortens US state names and finally turns single digits into words. Each rule has its own checkbox.
State abbreviations are applied longest-first so multi-word states such as New York are matched before shorter names.

article.heading: Know the limits
paragraphs: This is a formatting aid, not an authoritative style guide. The numeral rule converts any single digit, including day numbers in dates, so “May 5” becomes “May five”. Always review the output before publication.

name: Bank Statement Converter
title: Bank Statement Converter — Text and CSV Transactions
description: Parse pasted statement text or a text/CSV file into transactions with amounts, balances and running checks, then download CSV or QIF. PDF extraction and OCR are not included in this build.
intro: A conservative, local-only statement parser. Paste lines containing a date, description and amount, or open a text file, then review every row before downloading a result.
instructions: Paste statement text, load the sample or open a .txt/.csv file.
Choose a date order and statement type if automatic detection is wrong.
Click Parse transactions and inspect the table and balance check.
Download CSV or QIF when the rows look correct.

faqs.a: Not in this build. The reference application loads PDF.js and Tesseract.js from content delivery networks to extract text and run OCR. Those dependencies are not bundled here, so this tool deliberately accepts text and CSV only.
Only when opening, closing or running balances are present in the text. If no balances are found, the summary says there is nothing to check.
No. Parsing happens in your browser and no statement data is sent to a server.
This build exports CSV and QIF. The reference tool also offers XLSX, QuickBooks CSV, Xero CSV and OFX, which are not reproduced here.

article.heading: What it actually parses
paragraphs: Each non-empty line is scanned for a date, then for monetary amounts. Numeric and month-name dates are supported, with automatic or manual day/month ordering. Amounts can include currency symbols, thousands separators, negative signs, parentheses and CR/DR markers.
When two or more amounts are found, the first is treated as the transaction amount and the last as the running balance. The description is what remains after dates and amounts are removed.

article.heading: Balance checking and honesty
paragraphs: Balances are compared in integer cents between adjacent rows where a running balance is present. Rows that do not add up are marked so you can inspect them. A match is never claimed when there is no balance information.

This is a subset of the reference tool. It does not read PDF layouts, run OCR, infer debit and credit columns, repair scanned digits or produce spreadsheet workbooks. Review all output against the original statement before importing it anywhere.

name: Handwriting to Font Converter
title: Handwriting to Font Converter — Draw and Preview Glyphs
description: Draw handwriting glyphs on a canvas, preview them in a sentence and export a picture of the result. This scoped browser tool does not generate an installable OpenType font.
intro: Choose a character group, draw each glyph on the pad and build a preview from the shapes you have drawn. The download is a PNG picture, not a font file.
instructions: Pick a character group and select the character to draw.
Draw on the pad with the pen, or erase and undo strokes.
Type a phrase in the preview box and click Build preview.
Download the PNG preview if you are happy with the result.

faqs.a: No. Producing an installable OpenType font needs a contour tracer and CFF/OTF writer and is outside this build. This tool exports a PNG picture of your glyphs instead.

faqs.q: Is this the same as Text to Handwriting?
faqs.a: No. Text to Handwriting places typed text on notebook paper and exports PNG or PDF pages. This tool focuses on drawing individual letter shapes and previewing them as a sample.
No. Drawing, preview and export all happen in your browser.

article.heading: What this scoped tool does
paragraphs: The pad stores one drawing per character. The preview takes each drawn glyph, scales it to the chosen size and tiles the glyphs into a sample image. Undo and clear apply to the selected character only.
A PNG download is genuinely useful for mock-ups and for checking how a set of letters looks together, but it is not a font that an operating system can install.

article.heading: What the reference tool does
paragraphs: The supplied reference application includes a canvas editor, printable corner-marker templates, photo import with perspective correction, ink thresholding, contour tracing, per-character spacing controls and an embedded OpenType writer. Reproducing that stack faithfully would require a large, separately audited font pipeline.

This page keeps its own URL and states the difference plainly rather than implying that a font file is produced. For handwritten pages, use the preserved Text to Handwriting tool linked from the workspace.

name: Grammar & Spell Checker
title: Grammar & Spell Checker — Rule-Based English Proofreading in Your Browser
description: Check English text with local rules for common spelling, grammar, repeated words, spacing and clarity. Review suggestions, apply the ones you accept and keep the original text unchanged. No AI rewriting and no external or paid API.
intro: A transparent, rule-based English checker. It highlights probable mistakes, explains each suggestion and lets you accept or reject individually. It is deliberately honest about what local rules can and cannot do.
instructions: Paste English text or load a TXT, CSV, Markdown or DOCX file.
Choose a style emphasis and review the highlighted text and the suggestion list.
Select the suggestions to apply, or reject them all, then copy or download the corrected copy.

faqs.q: Is this an AI writing tool?
faqs.a: No. It is an explicitly rule-based, English-only checker. It uses local dictionaries and grammar rules, not a language model, and it does not rewrite your prose or invent new sentences.

faqs.q: Does it send my text anywhere?
faqs.a: No. Every check runs in your browser. There is no external, paid or third-party API, and no text is uploaded to a server.

No. It covers common spelling errors, frequent grammar patterns, repeated words, spacing and a few clarity rules. It is an aid to proofreading, not a replacement for a human reader or a specialist editor.

faqs.q: Does it work in languages other than English?
faqs.a: No. The dictionaries and rules are English only. Other languages will produce unreliable suggestions, so the tool states that scope plainly.

article.heading: What rule-based checking means
paragraphs: A rule-based checker does not understand your text the way a person does. Instead, it compares each word with a local word list and applies a small set of hand-written patterns for the mistakes that appear most often in English prose. When a pattern matches, the tool records the exact character range, the original text, a proposed replacement and a short explanation. You see those findings as highlights over the original text and as a list of suggestions underneath.

This design has a useful property: the result is predictable. The same input and the same style emphasis always produce the same suggestions, and every suggestion can be traced to a dictionary entry or a named rule. Nothing is generated, paraphrased or invented. The corrected copy is simply your own text with only the changes you chose to accept, applied from the end of the document backwards so earlier character offsets stay valid.

article.heading: The categories it checks
paragraphs: Spelling covers a curated set of frequently confused and commonly misspelled English words, such as their versus there, its versus it is, affect versus effect, and words like accomodate or occured. These are high-value targets because they survive spell-check in a surprising number of drafts: every candidate is a real word, so a generic dictionary check would not flag it.

Grammar rules look for repeated words, missing spaces after punctuation, extra spaces before punctuation, a missing capital at the start of a sentence and the common contraction confusions involving apostrophes. Repeated-word detection catches accidental doubles like the the or to to, which are easy to miss when rereading your own writing. Spacing rules catch the small but distracting errors that appear when text is pasted between applications.

Clarity suggestions are deliberately conservative. They point at wordy phrases that have a shorter common equivalent and at obvious filler, but they never rewrite a sentence. Style emphasis changes which suggestions are shown: an academic emphasis keeps formal phrasing, while a simple-English emphasis favours shorter alternatives. Choosing a style never changes your text on its own; it only affects the suggestions offered for review.

article.heading: Why the scope is English only
paragraphs: Spelling dictionaries, grammar patterns and style guidance are language specific. An English word list would flag perfectly correct words in French, Spanish or German, and English sentence rules do not apply to languages with different word order or no spaces between words. Rather than produce confidently wrong advice, this tool states that it checks English only. If you need another language, a dedicated checker for that language is the honest choice.

Even within English, local rules have clear limits. They cannot judge whether an argument is convincing, whether a tone suits its audience, or whether a passive construction was intentional. They do not understand context, irony or technical vocabulary, and they cannot detect a correctly spelled word used in the wrong sense. Treat every highlight as a question to answer, not an instruction to obey.

article.heading: Privacy and how to use the results
paragraphs: All work happens on your device. The page loads no dictionary service, calls no translation endpoint and uses no paid API. Text you paste stays in the browser session and is never transmitted. That matters for drafts, student work, legal notes and anything else you would rather not upload to a third-party service.

The safest workflow is to check a finished draft, read each suggestion in context, accept only the ones you agree with, then proofread the corrected copy once more. Use the highlighted view to find a problem and the suggestion list to understand why it was flagged. Rejecting all suggestions restores the original text, and the corrected copy can be copied or downloaded as a plain text file.

article.heading: What this tool is not
paragraphs: It is not a full natural-language-processing system, not an AI writing assistant and not a replacement for an editor. It does not analyse semantics, does not restructure paragraphs, does not generate alternatives beyond the fixed suggestions shown, and does not claim to improve your style in ways it cannot measure. Any page that promised those things from a small local rule set would be overstating what it can do.
The value here is a fast, private first pass that catches the mechanical errors people make most often. Used that way, it saves time and leaves the decisions in your hands.

name: Resume / CV Builder
title: Resume / CV Builder — 60 Templates and Local PDF Export
description: Build a professional resume or CV in the browser with 60 layout and colour combinations, local autosave and print-to-PDF export. This preserved standalone app keeps its original URL.
intro: The existing standalone application is linked directly from this directory. It stores resumes in the browser and exports through your browser’s print dialog; no account or upload is required.
instructions: Open the Resume Builder app from the directory card.
Choose a template and fill in your details.
Use the in-app preview and design controls, then print or save as PDF.

faqs.a: The card on the category and directory pages opens the preserved standalone application at /tools/resume-builder/index.html.

faqs.q: How does it differ from the reference resume builder?
faqs.a: The reference application offers 20 templates, PDF/DOCX export, resume import, a checker, job matching and one-page fitting. The preserved app offers 60 layout and colour combinations, local autosave and browser print-to-PDF. DOCX export, import, checking and job matching are not reproduced.
The preserved app saves resumes locally in the browser and does not upload their content.

article.heading: A preserved standalone application
paragraphs: Resume Builder already existed as a complete app when the reference tools were integrated. Its URL is kept so existing bookmarks continue to work, and it appears in search, categories and the sitemap through the central registry.
The reference version’s extra features are documented rather than faked. If you need DOCX export, resume import or job-keyword matching, this tool does not currently provide them.
